rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is entirely absent, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration to establish whether combining RNA and image data improves performance. This configuration isolates the effect of multimodal fusion (concat) with standard encoders (pca_n2000 and resnet50) and minimal aggregation, providing critical initial insights into the viability of multimodal approaches.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, concat fusion) achieves 52.66% accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (config_017) improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It directly builds on the current best configuration while exploring a key design choice (fusion method) that could significantly impact results. This balances exploitation of the current promising direction with targeted exploration of a critical component.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve ~0.526 accuracy. This experiment tests the impact of multiprofile setting combined with avgpool aggregation (a key design choice not yet tested in multimodal setups). It clarifies whether multiprofile improves performance and isolates the effect of aggregation method, balancing exploration of profile settings with exploitation of the base model architecture.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings and avgpool aggregation achieve the highest accuracy so far (config_018: 0.6186). This experiment tests whether switching from concat to weighted fusion in the same high-performing multimodal-multiprofile setup (pca_n2000 + resnet50) could further improve accuracy. It isolates the effect of fusion strategy while maintaining the proven effective components, balancing exploitation of the current top-performing architecture with targeted exploration of a key design choice.

The existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l image encoder with weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (0.635). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping the high-performing image encoder and fusion method, isolating the effect of aggregation. It balances exploitation of the current top-performing setup with exploration of a key design choice (aggregation method).

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile setups with imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_025) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.635). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated encoder) in this high-performing configuration improves accuracy further. It isolates the effect of RNA representation while keeping other critical components (image encoder, aggregation, fusion) consistent, maximizing exploitation of the current promising direction.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (e.g., config_037) achieve high validation accuracy (0.706). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping weighted fusion (a key component of config_037) improves performance. This isolates the effect of aggregation method, which is critical for understanding model behavior and potentially improving accuracy further.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, and imagenet_vit_l image encoder achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_039: 0.725). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt (a different architecture) while keeping the same image encoder, aggregation (transformer), and fusion (weighted) could further improve performance. It clarifies the impact of RNA encoder choice on accuracy, leveraging the strong foundation of the current top-performing configuration.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile models with scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation/weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests scgpt (a different RNA encoder) with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion, isolating the impact of RNA encoder choice while maintaining high-performing aggregation/fusion settings. It balances exploration of RNA encoder alternatives and exploits the strong performance of weighted fusion, maximizing the chance to find a slightly better configuration within the remaining budget.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests the same setup but with concat fusion instead of weighted fusion to isolate the effect of fusion method. It clarifies whether fusion strategy is critical for performance, leveraging the strong prior evidence of transformer aggregation's effectiveness.
